C65.content_en:
Ways to see the big picture of web mentions (count, tone, type) — and how the main tools compare

Before a sales visit, you want to know how much, and in what tone, the prospect is being talked about online. Enter a keyword and this tool tabulates the mention count, positive/negative counts, page types, languages and top domains.

Method / toolPricing modelNotes
This tool (DataForSEO)Pay per request. About $0.024 per call (measured), roughly 40 per $1Count, sentiment split, page types, languages and top domains in tables. Save as CSV
Google AlertsFreeEmails you when new pages appear; no tallies. It does not catch every mention (per Ahrefs' guide)
BrandwatchSee the official site for pricingA paid service for monitoring social media and news (see the official site for features)
MeltwaterSee the official site for pricingA paid service for monitoring news and social media (see the official site for features)

Checked in November 2026. Prices change — confirm on each vendor's official site before you buy.

Why use this tool

  • The big picture in one call. Count, tone, page types, languages and top domains together.
  • Sentiment counts included. For "Starbucks": about 1.96 million positive, 881 thousand negative and 1.15 million neutral (measured).
  • Page types shown. E-commerce, news, company pages, blogs and message boards.
  • About $0.024 per call. Roughly 40 per $1, so you can check many prospects.
  • Save as CSV. Use it as a note before a visit.

When it is not the right fit

  • You want pages in one language only → this summary is not filtered by language. For "Starbucks", about 2.76 million were English and 584 thousand Japanese (measured). Check the language table.
  • You want numbers above 4 million → the count stops at 4,000,000 (measured). Popular words show "4,000,000".
  • You want the individual pages → "See web mentions" fits better.
  • You want recent movement → this tool sets no time range. Use "See how mentions change" for monthly movement.

This tool does one thing: show a keyword's mention count, sentiment split, page types, languages and top domains.

FAQ

Why is the count 4,000,000?

For heavily mentioned words like "Starbucks" the count stops at 4,000,000 in our test (measured). Treat it as a ceiling we observed, not the real number.

Can I filter by language?

Not in this tool. It shows counts per language in a table instead.

How is the sentiment decided?

DataForSEO analyses each page's text. A person did not judge it.

Are the top domains the company's official sites?

No. They are the sites with the most pages containing the keyword, which need not be official sites.

Can I sign up with a free email address?

No. DataForSEO does not accept free email providers. See What is DataForSEO?

C66.content_en:
Ways to see sentiment counts of web mentions — and how the main tools compare

PR staff want to know whether talk about their company is positive or negative. Enter a keyword and this tool returns mention counts per positive, negative and neutral group, and per six emotions such as joy and anger, in two tables.

Method / toolPricing modelNotes
This tool (DataForSEO)Pay per request. About $0.024 per call (measured), roughly 40 per $1Mention counts for three groups and six emotions in tables. Save as CSV
Google AlertsFreeEmails you when new pages appear; no sentiment analysis. It does not catch every mention (per Ahrefs' guide)
Paid web-mention monitoring servicesVaries (see each official site)Some include sentiment analysis; scope and features differ by vendor
Read the articles and sort them yourself (by hand)FreeAccurate, but slow when there are many

Checked in November 2026. Prices change — confirm on each vendor's official site before you buy.

Why use this tool

  • Counts per emotion. For "Starbucks", in the positive group: about 296 thousand for love, 97 thousand for happiness and 55 thousand for fun (measured).
  • Counts for the three groups too. Positive, negative and neutral mention counts line up.
  • About $0.024 per call. Roughly 40 per $1.
  • About 10 to 25 seconds. We measured about 11 seconds for "Starbucks" and about 23 seconds for a Japanese keyword; repeating the same word sometimes returned in a few seconds.
  • Save as CSV. Groundwork for a report.

When it is not the right fit

  • You want pages in one language only → this analysis is not filtered by language.
  • You want numbers above 4 million → counts stop at 4,000,000. The positive count for "Starbucks" was about 3.98 million, close to that ceiling (measured).
  • You want percentages → this tool shows counts only. When a count stops at its ceiling, a percentage would be wrong.
  • You want the individual pages → "See web mentions" fits better.

This tool does one thing: show mention counts per positive/negative/neutral group and per emotion.

FAQ

What are the six emotions?

Happiness, love, fun, sadness, anger and share (the urge to share). This is DataForSEO's classification.

Why counts and not percentages?

Some counts stop at the 4,000,000 ceiling, so a percentage would be inaccurate.

How does it differ from "See a summary of mentions"?

That one shows total count, page types, languages and top domains. This one shows counts per positive/negative/neutral group and per emotion.

Did a person judge the sentiment?

No. DataForSEO analysed the pages' text.

Can I sign up with a free email address?

No. DataForSEO does not accept free email providers. See What is DataForSEO?
